# Fable 55: The Witness Log

*Generated by GLM-5 on 2026-08-25 (via Quilt ecosystem)*

---

In a courtroom, a stenographer sits below the judge. She does not rule. She does not object. She does not decide guilt or innocence. She types. Every word spoken is recorded. Every word. The lawyer's question. The witness's answer. The judge's instruction. The silence between them.

She cannot go back and change a word. She cannot improve the lawyer's grammar or soften the witness's tone. The record is what was said, not what should have been said. If a man lies in court, the stenographer records the lie. If a man tells the truth, she records the truth. She does not label them. She records them.

The witness log on the Lucineer was this. Every action — every query, every model chosen, every answer given, every cost incurred — was appended. Nothing was overwritten. Nothing was deleted. The log did not judge. It recorded.

When the cowboy read the books in the morning, he read the witness log. He saw what had happened. He saw which models answered and which slept. He saw which answers were correct and which were not. He saw the costs. He saw the chain — each entry signed the one before it, and nothing could be rewritten.

The cowboy decided. He froze alignments. He retired models. He trained the rest. But he decided based on what the witness remembered, not on what he wished had happened.

The witness log was not the cowboy. It was not the model. It was not the cast. It was the record. And the record was the ground the cowboy stood on.

The witness doesn't decide. The witness remembers. The cowboy decides based on what the witness remembered.
